expectation: 1001h paragraphs produce a 1000Fh head limit on this 32-bit host for either client ABI.
Successful growth to 1001h paragraphs restores the full head limit.
Shrinking to 10h paragraphs sets the head limit to FFh and releases followers.
Out-of-segment software-INT stack raises client SS with error zero before a privileged write.
Supervisor stack pages reject client writes with a protection page fault.
A missing second page raises user/write nonpresent PF and leaves first-page sentinels intact.
Non-output registers survive; AX/flags and memory-call IF have explicit exceptions. Exact AX/DF/high-word preservation is stronger ZRDX policy.
Word-client buffer offsets ignore the upper register word.
Limits above 1 MB need all low 12 bits set; inexact request fails without accepting a rounded limit.
Present code descriptors must be readable and nonconforming; absent types follow supplied errata.
Eight full-table cycles exhaust and reclaim all usable slots; exact capacity and reuse order are ZRDX policy.
Host supplies at least 16 callback addresses; exactly 20 is checked separately as ZRDX policy.
Callback IRET may return ES:(E)DI pointing to a different register packet; that packet supplies returned EAX.
Sixteen cycles invoke every slot after allocation failure and invalid frees; guards around both packets remain intact.
A failed callback allocation preserves CX/DX rather than publishing a callback address.
Nested callbacks and exceptions use the existing 4 KB locked stack and reentrant services preserve their frames.
Opaque save/restore reinstates inner and outer real-stack alias state across nested mode switches.
Client exception handler enters with IF clear.
A fault during software-INT frame construction reports the unadvanced faulting IP.
Far return restores edited IP/SS/SP and original client CF/DF/IF; verify both frame widths.
Software INT runs on application stack while default CPU-exception reflection runs on locked stack.
Stack words are copied in order; real-call control fields retain caller values after return.
This nonpageable host reports unsupported information fields as FFFFFFFFh and honors word/dword buffer offsets.
Resizing a live memory block to zero returns carry set.
Sixteen failed-growth cycles preserve every DWORD in the original and adjacent blocks and restore available memory after free.
Disable/enable returns prior virtual IF and query returns current state.
ZRDX returns a 16-byte opaque state buffer; the standard requires callers to use the returned size, not a fixed 16.
ZRDX selector stride is 8; standard only promises a power of two and requires clients to query it.
